extracted.intended_audience: general-circulation newspaper readers interested in international and national news (Cold War-era politics, diplomacy, and legal affairs)
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-item newspaper page (AP/press coverage) reporting on postwar diplomatic arrangements, State Department positions, Cold War developments, and major U.S. court cases. Includes excerpts of legal/international-agreement text and courtroom jury-instruction summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison arrangements with other governments
rubrics_metrics.description: “the necessary liaison with the Governments of other nations especially interested will be ensured by the appointment by such Governments of appropriate missions to the Council of the High Commission having access, by procedures to be determined, to its subordinate bodies and to the German Government.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that liaison is to be ensured via appointment of missions to the High Commission Council with access (procedures to be determined) to subordinate bodies and the German Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation of United Nations organizations in Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: “United Nations organizations and specialized agencies may operate in the federal republic of Germany on such terms as may be agreed by the Council.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants authority for UN and specialized agencies to operate in the Federal Republic of Germany subject to terms agreed by the Council of the High Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official languages of the High Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: “The official languages of the High Commission shall be English and French.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds that authoritative German texts of documents shall be provided as necessary (i.e., English and French are official; German versions provided when needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution, authenticity, and entry-into-force of agreement texts
rubrics_metrics.description: “In witness whereof the ... agreement has been duly executed by the respective representatives ... in triplicate in the French and English languages, each text being equally authentic and shall come into effect on the date of the entry into force of the occupation statute.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: agreements executed in triplicate in French and English with equal authenticity; the agreement's legal effect begins upon the occupation statute's entry into force.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. legal position on Chinese port-closing orders (blockade standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: United States position: it “cannot admit the legality” of barriers against shipping into Communist-held ports “unless the Chinese Government declares and maintains an effective blockade.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State Department instructed the embassy at Canton to reply that, despite friendly feelings, the U.S. cannot recognize port-closing orders as legal unless an effective blockade is declared and maintained; Secretary Acheson cited historical precedents and framed this as reserving rights of American citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal-intent standard for espionage conviction (Coplon case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge's instruction: convict only if the defendant took secret government papers with intent to pass them to a foreign power and intended or had reason to believe the information would be used to the injury of the United States or to the advantage of a foreign country; the injury need not be great and any slight injury or small advantage would suffice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains essential elements: (1) deliberate taking of documents, (2) intent to deliver to a foreign power, and (3) belief that the documents would injure the U.S. or advantage a foreign country. If documents were taken for personal use without such intent, verdict should be not guilty. The judge emphasized that the required ‘intent’ is central and that even slight injury/advantage meets the statutory threshold.
